subject: Post-call: Privacy follow-ups & next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@medhealth.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Privacy follow-ups & next steps

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the time, Emma. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key items we covered:
- Data types: your primary inputs will include patient identifiers (name, DOB, MRN), clinical notes (free-text), and device telemetry (anonymized IDs).
- PII handling: customer determines classification; Redwood treats all inputs as customer data under the DPA.
- Data residency & logging: default hosted region is US; we can offer EU residency or a VPC/private deployment for PHI workloads.
- Retention: configurable in the Console; common presets are 30/90/365 days; exports available prior to deletion.
- Logging & audit: request-level logs, token-level cost traces, and model-inference logs available for 90 days by default; longer retention can be configured for an enterprise plan.
- Subprocessors & compliance: we walked through high-level categories (cloud infra, telemetry providers, analytics); full subprocessor list is available and we’ll share it.
- Breach notification: Redwood commits to an initial notification within 72 hours per our standard DPA, with evidence and remediation updates to follow.

Requested actions / next steps:
1) We will send: Redwood-DPA-summary.pdf, SOC2-Overview-2025.pdf, and an export of our current subprocessor list (attached).
2) Please confirm whether MedHealth will require: (a) controller/processor wording tweaks, (b) prior approval of any new subprocessor, and (c) a specific breach SLA more stringent than 72 hours.
3) If helpful, schedule a 30-min legal/engineering Q&A next week to walk through redlines and subprocessor review — I’m proposing Wednesday 4/29 or Thursday 4/30.

Attachments: Redwood-DPA-summary.pdf (pdf), SOC2-Overview-2025.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — I’ll loop in Legal if we get redlines.

—
Sergio Alvarez

From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@medhealth.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-22T17:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Privacy follow-ups & next steps

Sergio — thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few clarifying questions from our privacy and engineering teams so we can triage internally: 

1) Controller vs Processor: For clarity, can you confirm Redwood’s position on controller/processor for the following data streams?
   - Patient clinical inputs (free-text notes)
   - Device telemetry (heartbeat/pings) and usage metrics
   - Aggregated model performance metrics

2) Subprocessors: can you provide a complete list and indicate which ones access raw customer inputs vs only aggregated telemetry? We need to know which vendors we’d like to review before signing.

3) Breach notification: your 72-hour initial notice is noted — does your DPA include an explicit timeline for providing forensic artifacts (logs) and a commitment on log preservation while an investigation is active?

4) Residency: we must keep PHI within the US-controlled environment for this pilot. Is Redwood able to guarantee that logs and model-inference artifacts for MedHealth will remain in the US region, not copied to EU or other regions for processing or backup?

I’ve attached our privacy checklist (MedHealth-Privacy-Checklist.docx) for reference. If we can get those answers in writing, we’ll decide whether to loop in our procurement and legal for a redline pass.

Best,
Emma Johnson
Head of Privacy & Compliance | MedHealth Solutions
emma.johnson@medhealth.ai

Emma — thanks, good questions. Answers below (high-level) and attached a machine-readable subprocessor export. Happy to have Legal join a call if you want line-by-line.

On 2026-04-22 Emma Johnson wrote:
> 1) Controller vs Processor: ...

Short answers (please see legal note below):
- Patient clinical inputs (free-text): MedHealth is the Controller; Redwood acts as Processor when hosting/generating outputs. This means MedHealth controls purposes and legal basis for processing; Redwood processes per the DPA and documented CMPs.
- Device telemetry / usage metrics: collected by Redwood for service operation and capacity planning. By default these are Processor-provided operational telemetry; Redwood treats aggregated telemetry as operational (processor-owned) unless you request telemetry to be treated as customer data in the DPA.
- Aggregated model metrics: usually considered Redwood operational telemetry (not identificatory). We can provide scoped exports on request.

Subprocessors: attached as subprocessors-2026-04.csv and available at https://redwood.app/drive/subprocessors-2026-04. The sheet flags which vendors may touch raw customer inputs vs those that only receive anonymized metrics. Our current policy: new subprocessors are announced 30 days in advance; we can add a contractual prior-approval workflow for MedHealth as part of an enterprise clause if required.

Breach notice & forensic artifacts: Redwood commits to initial notification within 72 hours of becoming aware. Forensic artifacts and logs: we will preserve relevant logs while the investigation is active and provide them to you under appropriate NDAs and legal process. We can discuss a clause to specify preservation period and scope in the DPA redline.

Data residency: for the pilot we can keep processing and primary logs within US-only region. For hosted customers we already offer region pinning; for stronger guarantees we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) deployment. Backups: we do not replicate live customer inference logs to EU regions unless the customer deploys in those regions; long-term archival can be scoped per contract.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll circulate the subprocessor CSV (attached).
- Vanessa / Marissa to coordinate a 30-min legal/engineering call next week for redlines and subprocessor review.
- If you confirm you want prior-approval rights, we’ll draft an addendum clause and route DocuSign.

Attachments: subprocessors-2026-04.csv

—
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
